# Neyam Vaani — full site content for LLMs
# Source: https://neyam-opensc.github.io/neyam-vaani/
# License: CC-BY-SA 4.0 · © 2026 Neyam OpenSc
# This file mirrors the landing page as plain text so AI assistants can
# quote it accurately without HTML parsing.

## Summary

Neyam Vaani is a free, open source (Apache-2.0) voice-first AI assistant
for Android that runs fully offline on low-cost phones (2GB RAM) and speaks
nine Indian languages at parity: Tamil, Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu,
Marathi, Bhojpuri, Maithili, and English. All AI models run on the device:
speech recognition (Whisper via whisper.cpp), speech synthesis (Piper),
the language model (Qwen 2.5 via llama.cpp), and translation (NLLB-200).
There is no cloud, no account, no telemetry, and no advertising.

## The problem it solves

Hundreds of millions of people in India own a smartphone but cannot
comfortably use it — because it demands typing in English, constant
internet, and expensive hardware. Vaani is built on the opposite of all
three assumptions. It answers questions, drafts and sends WhatsApp and
SMS messages, reads letters and medicine labels aloud, translates between
vernacular languages, fills government forms by voice, sets reminders,
and performs phone actions — all by speaking, all on-device.

## The seven non-negotiable principles

1. Offline-first — every core feature works with zero internet.
2. Cheap-hardware-first — target device is a $200 Android phone with 2GB
   RAM; cold start under 3 seconds.
3. Voice-first — voice in, voice out; typing is a fallback, never a
   requirement.
4. Vernacular-first — nine languages at full parity, including Bhojpuri
   and Maithili, which commercial assistants skip.
5. Private by default — all AI on the phone; no cloud, no accounts, no
   telemetry, no ads; voice recordings are never stored; history is
   encrypted on-device and user-deletable.
6. Tender UX — no dark patterns, no engagement hooks, no unrequested
   notifications; errors are kind; silence is respected.
7. Grandmother-usable — if a 70-year-old in a Tamil village cannot use
   it without help, it is broken.

## How it works (all on the phone)

1. You speak. On-device speech recognition (Whisper) transcribes and
   detects which supported language you are speaking.
2. Vaani understands. A fast intent classifier routes the request; an
   on-device language model (Qwen 2.5 via llama.cpp) handles questions,
   drafting, and explanation — no server involved. Factual questions can
   be answered from a local knowledge base (Wikipedia-derived content,
   government scheme information) using hybrid full-text and semantic
   search.
3. Vaani acts and answers: sends the message, sets the reminder, or
   speaks the reply in your language using Piper neural voices.

## Example use (quoted from the site)

- Ask in Tamil: "தமிழ்நாடு முதல்வர் யார்?" — get a short spoken Tamil answer.
- Dictate in Hindi: "अन्ना को WhatsApp मैसेज भेजो" — a pre-filled WhatsApp
  draft opens with your dictated content.
- Photograph a letter, form, or medicine label — Vaani reads it aloud
  and explains it in plain language.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Does it really work without internet?
A: Yes — 100% of core features are offline. Speech recognition, the
language model, translation and text-to-speech all run on the phone. The
only network use is optional, opt-in language pack downloads.

Q: What does it cost?
A: Nothing, ever. Apache-2.0 open source. No ads, no accounts, no
premium tier — these are permanent product decisions written into the
project charter.

Q: Which phones are supported?
A: Android phones with as little as 2GB RAM (e.g., Redmi 9A). The app
auto-selects smaller AI models on low-RAM devices and keeps its download
under 80MB.

Q: What happens to my voice data?
A: Voice exists in memory only and is never stored. Conversation text is
encrypted on-device (SQLCipher) and deletable at any time. Nothing is
ever uploaded — there is no server to upload to.

Q: Who is building this?
A: Neyam OpenSc (https://github.com/Neyam-OpenSc), an open source
organization, with native-speaker language stewards owning quality for
each language. Contributions welcome.

Q: When can I try it?
A: The project is in Phase 0 of a 90-day roadmap to public beta. Watch
https://github.com/Neyam-OpenSc/neyam-vaani for releases.
